best_for: Linux desktop users, KDE Plasma ones especially, who want an mpv-based video player with a normal window, menus and a playlist instead of mpv's bare config files.

points.title: mpv inside, a regular app outside
points.text: Haruna is built on libmpv, so it plays what mpv plays, wrapped in a KDE interface. You can still send raw mpv commands at startup or from a shortcut if you want mpv's tweaks.

points.title: Playlists fill themselves
points.text: Open one episode and Haruna lists the other videos in the same folder, so a whole season plays in order without building a playlist by hand.

points.title: Small conveniences that add up
points.text: There is a thumbnail preview on the seek bar, rebindable shortcuts and mouse buttons, and an option to skip chapters whose titles contain words you choose, such as intros.

points.title: Online video through yt-dlp
points.text: Paste a link to an online video and Haruna plays it through youtube-dl or yt-dlp, without opening a browser.

points.title: Linux is home, Windows is newer
points.text: KDE's download page lists only Linux, through distribution packages and Flathub. A Windows installer exists for x64, per-user or all-users, and the Windows listing here keeps just 3 versions. No macOS build is listed.

points.title: Official Flatpak
points.text: The Flathub build for x64 and Arm64 is verified through KDE. Haruna is free under the GPL 3.0 or later, with no account or ads.
